name: Albert Yan
headline: Biochemistry graduate building computational tools for structural biology — and auditing how they get evaluated.
summary:
I studied biochemistry at the University of Washington, entering through the Robinson Center for Young Scholars after tenth grade. Alongside the degree I spent about 2,500 hours in direct patient care as a CNA and a one-on-one caregiver, and worked in an artificial kidney dialysis lab on the design of a portable dialysis system.

I now write software to study proteins computationally. Most of what I have learned has come from measuring my own methods rather than from the pipelines themselves: that a date-based held-out test set is mostly not held out, that an uncertain structure prediction is a distribution rather than a structure, and that a benchmark's apparent model failures are often failures of target selection. Those findings changed how the tooling works, and several of them contradicted what I expected going in.

I am headed toward graduate work at the intersection of machine learning and biomedical systems.
